subject: Throughput-sensitivity review & dedicated sizing asks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — throughput sensitivity & deployment path (asks)

Samir — thanks for the demo today. Short recap and a few clarification asks so we can size a dedicated pool and scope a short POC.

Key points from the call:
- You indicated production goals are latency-sensitive for the user-facing endpoint, and you prefer a dedicated path for predictable throughput and data isolation.
- Current estimate: ~120 req/s peak across global traffic (you noted bursts into the mid-200s), multi-tenant (separate tenants per product line).
- Compliance: SOC 2 and contractual SLA obligations — you may require a VPC/private deployment later.

Clarifying asks (we need these to run sizing estimates):
1) TPS definition: is 120 req/s measured at request rate (calls/sec) or token/sec? Please confirm 95th/99th percentile rates you care about.
2) Token mix: what is the typical prompt/context token length and average generated tokens per request? If you have a sample histogram or logs, upload a 1k-sample.
3) Concurrency expectations: do you expect simultaneous long-running completions (e.g., streaming outputs) per tenant? Any tenant-level p95 concurrency targets?
4) Acceptable p95 latency SLO (end-to-end) and tail target (p99) so we can choose GPU flavor.
5) Preferred GPU family tradeoff: cost sensitivity vs. latency sensitivity (A100 vs H100) — any internal constraints or procurement preferences?

Attached: capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (template we discussed) and a short POC proposal (proto_poc_plan.pdf).

Next steps:
- If you can drop a 1k-sample of payloads (anonymized) and confirm the two latency SLOs above, we’ll run microbenchmarks and present two capacity profiles (A100 cost-optimal and H100 latency-optimal) with estimated GPU counts and concurrency per GPU.
- Tentative POC timeline: 3 weeks for benchmarks + 4 weeks pilot if we align.

Thanks — I’ll loop Karthik in for the microbench plan.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@blueharbor.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueHarbor AI Engineering <eng@blueharbor.ai>
Date: 2027-09-09T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — throughput sensitivity & deployment path (asks)

Hey Marcus — thanks for the clear notes. A few answers below to help you size: 

- TPS definition: our SLA is defined in requests/sec. The 95th percentile request rate we care about is 120 req/s (SLO), but we regularly see bursts to ~220 req/s for short windows (1–2 minutes) during traffic spikes.
- Token mix: Typical prompt/context is small — median 40 tokens; generated tokens average 180 tokens. So roughly 20% prompt / 80% generation by token count.
- Concurrency: For the main product line (tenant A) peak concurrency target is ~40 simultaneous completions. Other tenants are smaller (5–10 each). We’d like isolation between tenants but happy to start with capacity pooling + soft tenant limits.
- Latency SLO: p50 target 120–200ms; p95 target 400ms end-to-end (client-facing). We know p99 will be higher and we want guidance on tail mitigation.
- GPU preference: cost matters; procurement has historically leaned toward A100, but for this product we might accept H100 if the latency improvement is material. Open to your recommendation.

I’ll upload a sanitized sample log to the Drive link you provided by EOD today. Also open to starting with a hosted pilot to validate model latencies before committing to a dedicated reserved pool.

— Samir
VP Product
BlueHarbor AI

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — throughput sensitivity & deployment path (analysis)

Marcus / Vanessa — quick sizing sketch based on Samir’s numbers. High-level notes before we formalize: 

- Workload profile: 120 req/s p95 with bursts ~220 req/s. Token-weighted load skews heavy on generation (avg ~180 tokens). This increases per-request GPU time vs short prompts.
- Latency SLO: p95 400ms end-to-end implies aggressive batching limits. For many models, achieving p95 400ms at 180-gen tokens will push toward H100 for single-GPU latency headroom, especially if you want p50 around 150ms.
- Suggested approach (two tracks):
  * Latency-first: H100 cluster (N GPUs) sized to keep p95 < 400ms under 120 req/s steady, with headroom for 2x burst absorption via autoscale/burst capacity.
  * Cost-first: A100 cluster with higher GPU count and more aggressive batching to optimize tokens/sec; expect p95 to increase ~1.5–2x vs H100 for same steady load.

Rough numbers (very early):
- H100 path: ~8–12 H100 GPUs to cover steady 120 req/s at average 180 gen tokens with p95 ~400ms (depends on model variant and quantization).
- A100 path: ~14–18 A100 GPUs for similar token throughput but with higher p95 latency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marcus to schedule microbench window (we need representative prompt + model variant).
2) Run a small perf bench (single-GPU and 4-GPU) and fill the provided capacity workbook with observed tokens/sec and p95 latencies. I’ve attached perf-bench-results-hypothesis.md with our expected throughput ranges to baseline the runs.
3) Produce a short decision memo (A100 vs H100) with estimated monthly unit cost at target throughput.

I’ll own the bench plan — happy to sync with Samir for any constraints (e.g., fixed model version, use of KV cache, or quantization allowance).

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-09T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — throughput sensitivity & deployment path (action items)

Samir — appreciate the quick answers. Action items and proposed timeline: 

1) You: upload the sanitized 1k-sample payloads + confirm whether we should include streaming completions in the bench (you can drop them to the Drive link). Target: EOD today.
2) Marcus/Karthik: schedule a 2-hour perf bench window next week (we’ll propose Wed/Thu morning PT). We’ll run both A100 and H100 microbenchmarks, capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, and populate the workbook.
3) After bench (3 business days), we’ll deliver two capacity profiles (latency-first H100 and cost-first A100) and a recommended POC scope for a 4-week pilot.

If that sounds good I’ll send a calendar invite with 3 candidate windows. Also attaching the workbook and POC plan for your review.

Thanks — looking forward to the bench data.

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
